chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh ibn Nusayr, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abdallah ibn Zurara who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: convey my salutations to your father and say to him: … and your two sons al-Hasan and al-Husayn brought me your letter, may Allah guard, defend, watch over and protect them because of the goodness of their father, the way He had protected the two boys …

key_terms.الْحَسَنُ وَالْحُسَيْنُ: Al-Hasan and Al-Husayn (the two sons of Zurara)
key_terms.الْغُلَامَيْنِ: The two boys (referring to the orphans in Surah Al-Kahf)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the sons of Zurara and their father's letter?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kashi’s *Rijal* highlights the spiritual status of Abdallah ibn Zurara’s sons, Hasan and Husayn, by linking their divine protection to their father’s righteousness and drawing a parallel to the Quranic story of the two boys. The Imam’s prayer emphasizes the concept of *kafalah* (guardianship) and the intergenerational merit (*fadilah*) in Shia tradition, where the piety of the father safeguards the offspring. This narrative reinforces the scholarly view that the Ahl al-Bayt’s blessings extend to the families of their close companions, particularly the Zurara family, who were prominent in transmitting hadith.
